Alex Chen: quick signal — after yesterday's kernel-router tweak I'm seeing a regression on Mistral-7B in prod-like perf runs. p50 token latency at seq=256, batch=1 went from ~48ms -> ~72ms. throughput down ~20%. :confused:
Maria Gomez: ouch. any single change that stands out? kernel selection log?
Alex Chen: yes, router now prefers tiled matmul kernel for >64 heads by default. profiler shows heavier time in kernel_select + matmul_tiled than before. perf-bot: profiler snapshot attached ->
perf-bot: ```
PROFILE: model=mistral-7b, seq=256, batch=1
  total_tokens: 25600
  kernel_select: 180ms (was 120ms)
  matmul_tiled: 220ms (was 150ms)
  kv_cache_warmup: 30ms
  prefix_cache_hit_rate: 93%
  end_to_end_p50: 72ms
```
Jon Patel: does the router check head/kvdims or just n_head threshold? we switched to head-based heuristic but maybe missed kv dim parity.
Sasha Ivanov: router checks n_head and dtype, but not kv_dim alignment. if kv_dim % tile_size != 0 tiled kernel gets inefficient. seen it before with mixtral conversions. @Maria Gomez can you surface the HF configs that failed conversion last week?
Maria Gomez: attaching config snippet from failing HF model ->
Maria Gomez: ```json
{
  "n_heads": 32,
  "d_model": 4096,
  "kv_channels": 128,
  "rope_scaling": { "type": "linear", "factor": 1.0 }
}
```
Maria Gomez: conversion script logged a warning: `safetensors metadata missing: \"dtype\"` and later `KeyError: 'rotary_emb_scale'` during weight mapping.
Alex Chen: that explains it — missing rotary metadata caused us to fallback to a generic RoPE handler that reinterprets dims and triggers different kernel selection path. fallback adds extra checks in kernel_select and forces slower matmul.
Jon Patel: two things: (1) conversion script should inject explicit `rotary_emb_scale` metadata into safetensors, (2) router should do cheap kv_dim % tile_size check before choosing tiled kernel.
Sasha Ivanov: agreed. propose patch: if seq>128 and kv_dim % TILE != 0, use matmul_strided (fallback) else tiled. also add a fast-path to check prefix cache hit rate to avoid rerouting during warmup.
Alex Chen: also observed batching heuristics interacting badly: continuous batching window extended from 8ms->20ms in that deploy, so small concurrency got coalesced and then kernel router saw mixed seq/kv shapes and picked conservative kernel.
Maria Gomez: can we temporarily revert the batching window change? customers on dedicated noticed latency spikes. @deploy-bot any chance we can rollback just that config on staging?
deploy-bot: rollback config flag set for staging; rolling back batching_window to 8ms now. :white_check_mark:
perf-bot: quick follow-up run after rollback (staging):
perf-bot: ```
PROFILE: model=mistral-7b, seq=256, batch=1 (after rollback)
  kernel_select: 125ms
  matmul_tiled: 155ms
  prefix_cache_hit_rate: 95%
  end_to_end_p50: 50ms
```
Alex Chen: much better. still want longer-term fixes: conversion script metadata defaults, router kv_dim alignment check, and add a small heuristic that avoids switching kernels mid-request when prefix cache hot.
Jon Patel: I'll open PR for router change + tests that emulate odd kv_dims. I'll include a micro-benchmark that compares matmul_tiled vs matmul_strided for kv_dim mod TILE != 0.
Sasha Ivanov: I'll update conversion tool to populate `rotary_emb_scale` and `dtype` in safetensors metadata and add a validation step that warns on missing fields and fails CI on new model onboarding.
Maria Gomez: I'll run a sweep on onboarding queue to re-convert any models that had missing metadata. also will add an eval that checks end_to_end p50 for seq=128/256.
Alex Chen: action items summary: 1) Jon -> router PR (kv_dim check + no mid-request switches) 2) Sasha -> conversion metadata + CI validation 3) Maria -> re-convert queue + perf sweep 4) Ops -> keep batching_window at 8ms for now.
Alex Chen: thanks team. if anyone sees another regression, ping me directly. :eyes:
